title: THE SAME KNIFE CUTS DIFFERENTLY
question: For the same matched edge, input, and output anchor, is the effect of substituting the opposite-sex edge weight approximately reciprocal across MORTY and LILITH backgrounds, or does network background alter the functional consequence of that same structural difference?

definitions.normalized_asymmetry: 0 when both deltas are exactly zero; otherwise abs(delta_morty + delta_lilith) / (abs(delta_morty) + abs(delta_lilith))
definitions.sign_relation: OPPOSITE when product < 0; SAME when product > 0; ZERO_INVOLVED otherwise

primary_metric.name: integrated_positive_voltage_context_residual
primary_metric.reason: Uses the raw reciprocity residual so tiny near-zero effects cannot look important merely because a normalized ratio is large.

ranking.purpose: future scalar follow-up candidate generation only

sq03c_verification_subset.purpose: Report the same frozen metrics on pairs for which both subject counterfactuals have already been independently scalar-verified.

claim_boundary: SQ-03D measures context dependence inside the frozen MoscaQuant matched central-brain model. A nonzero reciprocity residual means that the same male/female edge-weight difference has different modeled consequences when embedded in the two matched network backgrounds. It does not establish a biological sex mechanism, organism-level behavior, population-level statistical significance, intelligence differences, or financial utility.
